answer.rationale: Contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew, so deferral risks a stop at 94% volume/no buffer; incumbent has refused price and c4/c6-style renegotiation is blocked this cycle, while the low-cost quote alone meets the 18% mandate. c2 supports the low-cost vendor (sharp unit-cost cut, quick onboarding, accurate invoicing), but it is a last-year record, so I verify it before committing and limit the move to a guarded, phased cutover rather than a broad rollover, respecting c1 (incumbent stability) and c3 (avoid single-point failure) by not collapsing to one unproven source at full volume. Delivery risk is flagged because any primary transition at 94% committed volume with no buffer can raise TCO via expedites/line stoppage even if unit price falls.
